A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same decayed identity shortcut method. Their main text, equations, six corresponding figures, four tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet linear-probing experiments, architectural ablations, reconstruction examples, and supervised and unsupervised feature-rank analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports revised ImageNet-1K results and retains original ImageNet-100 ablations, qualitative evaluations, and supervised feature-rank experiments, including in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The depth-dependent shortcut scaling, encoder-only application, encoder-decoder skip connections, and residual zero initialization remain unchanged. The architectural diagrams and method equations describe the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1K and ImageNet-100 representations and retain the supervised ImageNet-subset experiment. Reconstruction and supervised analyses move into Appendix B without introducing or removing dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 explicitly adds the unscaled residual configuration, scoring 76.5%, to the decay-scheme comparison in Table 3b. This baseline was already reported in Table 2, but its participation in Table 3b is new. Table 1 retains the same comparator methods.

E3.justification: The primary ImageNet-1K probing protocol is replaced: v1 documents four cached feature views per image and a custom 200-epoch AdamW probe, whereas v2 Appendix A.2 reports using the original MAE evaluation protocol, including random augmentation. This substantially changes the reported evaluation procedure for the headline benchmark; pretraining and ImageNet-100 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The same decay-rate, architecture-size, skip-connection, scaling-placement, reconstruction, embedding, and feature-rank analyses remain. The supervised and reconstruction analyses are relocated, and Table 3b redisplays an existing baseline result without introducing a new ablation question.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes MAE/ours accuracy from 67.3/72.3% to 67.8/72.7%. Table 4 changes ImageNet-1K results at alpha_min 0.5/0.6/0.7 from 69.4/72.3/68.5% to 69.8/72.7/68.9%. These accompany a protocol change, not demonstrated same-setting gains. Other tabulated results and rank curves remain unchanged; v2 Section 4.1 still quotes the old Table 1 values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including the expanded shortcut recurrence, decay schedule, and effective-rank definition, are mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The title narrows the framing from self-supervised abstract feature learning generally to masked autoencoders specifically. The abstract and introduction update the headline accuracy comparison, while retaining the central shortcut-decay and low-rank-correlation claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a contrastive-learning applicability limitation, arguing that low-rank bias conflicts with MoCo-v3's repulsive objective, and explains how learned scaling can compensate for scaling the residual branch. Conversely, its rewritten rank discussion omits v1's explicit qualification about alpha_min 0.7 and 0.8 producing higher-rank outliers, although the curves remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly reports four NVIDIA A40 GPUs and approximately 20/200 training hours for ImageNet-100/1K. The detailed custom ImageNet-1K probing recipe and its runtime comparison are replaced by a reference to the original MAE protocol. The relocated supervised experiment also loses its explicit 10-class subset specification.

R1.justification: The related-work coverage and distinct cited works remain unchanged; the additional U-Net bibliography entry duplicates an existing work. However, the new contrastive-learning discussion refines the method's positioning relative to MoCo-v3 and argues for focusing on masked autoencoders.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Selective changes include the title, contribution bullets, clarified decay terminology, a condensed feature-rank discussion, and reorganized appendices containing the relocated reconstruction and supervised analyses.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted with different page geometry, typography, headers, and figure/table placement. Figure 1 is redrawn and recolored, plot legends are reformatted, reconstruction and supervised figures move to the appendix, and Table 3b gains a baseline row. The other visualized evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves scope clarity, standardizes the stated ImageNet-1K evaluation, and adds useful compute information. These benefits coexist with inconsistent headline results between Table 1 and Section 4.1, removal of the rank-outlier qualification, and reduced experimental detail. With the method and most evidence unchanged, these opposing reporting and interpretive changes do not establish a reliable net quality improvement or deterioration.
